key_insight: The paper learns ab initio phase-field models by deriving the mesoscopic equation from molecular dynamics and using neural networks to fit the remaining free energy and mobility terms.
engineering_relevance: This enables microstructure evolution simulations with near-quantum accuracy at mesoscopic length and time scales, useful for predicting phase stability and phase separation in materials and planetary mixtures.
method: Derive phase-field dynamics from a Mori-Zwanzig projection of molecular dynamics onto species-density fields.
Parameterize unknown nonlocal free energy and mobility with neural networks.
Train on short MD trajectories generated by machine-learning interatomic potentials with ab initio accuracy.
evidence_signal: Validated on iron-boron and hydrogen-helium systems, including prediction of FeB4 instability at ambient pressure but stabilization at 10 GPa and helium-rain simulations up to a 2.2-million-atom-equivalent column.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and transferability of the learned neural free-energy and mobility terms, so extrapolation beyond the training compositions and conditions may be unreliable.
